children: Malaysian palm oil futures slipped on Monday, pressured by declines in Dalian palm olein and Chicago soyoil, with weaker crude oil prices adding to the downside as traders awaited confirmation of Malaysia's proposed export duty waiver.
The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for January delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange lost 25 ringgit, or 0.52%, to 4,793 ringgit ($1,173.60) a metric ton at the close.
"The futures opened gap lower following weakness in energy prices and in related vegetable oil futures," said Anilkumar Bagani, head of research at Mumbai-based vegetable oil broker Sunvin Group.
"However, the main catalyst is the absence of any confirmation of an export duty waiver from Malaysia and (the) market (is) seen erasing the news premium from the palm oil prices."
Dalian's most active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 0.13%, while its palm oil contract
dropped 0.52%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were down 0.43%.
Palm oil tracks rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Crude oil prices fell on Monday after surging last week to near six-month highs, amid hopes of easing hostilities between the United States and Iran, although persistent attacks on key producer Saudi Arabia kept investors wary.
Weaker crude oil futures make palm a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
Cargo surveyors estimated that Malaysian palm oil product exports for October 1-25 rose between 46.9% and 67.7% from a month earlier.
The ringgit, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.05% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.
